## Note Well.

Since the citations <note>original: "Citationes"</note> for the pages in the current treatise do not match those in the <term>Chemical Treatise</term> <note>Basilius Valentinus's "Chymische Schriften," a foundational work of early chemistry and alchemy.</note> of Basilius Valentinus <note>A legendary figure in alchemy, purportedly a 15th-century monk, though his works were likely written in the early 1600s.</note>, which was published for the fifth time in Hamburg in the year 1740, the cited passages have been recorded here in the margin <note>original: "ex margine"</note> with their proper page numbers <note>original: "folia," referring to the numbered leaves of a book.</note> according to the aforementioned Hamburg edition. It is presumed that this author recorded the page numbers according to the very old edition of Basilius's writings from the year 1700, which is the third edition <gloss>3rd</gloss>; I found this to be the case once that version came into my possession.

<summary>This handwritten note explains a correction to the manuscript's page references, which originally matched a 1700 edition of Basilius Valentinus's work rather than the 1740 Hamburg edition.</summary>

# ALCHEMY UNVEILED
## REVISED AND ENLARGED,
->Or:<-

That which until now was never rightly believed, but through experience
is now truly confirmed and placed beyond all doubt,
newly overseen and augmented or in many ways better explained

# Wonders of Nature,

->Together with an attached<-
Detailed description of the [gold-bearing materials] found not far from Zwickau in
Meissen at Nieder-Hohendorff and other surrounding
places, titled:

# Golden Sands,

->Presenting,<-

How, from various materials sincerely named herein,
as well as in various ways and manners, in deed and in truth,
a <term>Universal Medicine</term> <note>A hypothetical substance, often synonymous with the Philosopher's Stone, capable of curing all diseases and perfecting metals.</note> (for the human body and for the improvement of metals)
is to be prepared;

->As also<-

That despite all the writings of the <term>Philosophers</term> <note>original: "Philosophorum"; here referring specifically to alchemical authorities.</note>, and aside from the
<term>Universal Source</term> <note>original: "Fonte universali"; the primary source or principle of alchemical transformation.</note>, a highly useful and greatly
<gloss>profit-bearing</gloss> "Particular" <note>In alchemy, a 'Particular' refers to a process that successfully transforms a specific base metal into gold or silver, rather than the 'Universal' work which transforms all matter.</note> is nonetheless to be attained;

**All produced after long-term diligence devoted to**
**chemical study** <note>original: "Studio Chymico"</note>, partly seen with my own eyes, partly
performed with my own hands, and despite the "Philosophical Curse" <note>A traditional warning in alchemical literature against revealing secrets to the unworthy or uninitiated.</note> cited by many,
published for significant reasons and to provide a good
example for others to follow with similar experiments/

->By<-
->**J. N. v. E. I.**<-
->Roman Knight and <term>Count Palatine</term> <note>original: "Comite Palat."; a title of nobility often associated with the Holy Roman Empire.</note><-

---

->**Leipzig and Stralsund**,<-
Published by Samuel Gottlieb Lochmann, In the Year 1728.

## New Preface.

### To the Reader, Honored with All Dignity!

Regarding the new edition of this current <term>treatise<note>original: "Tractat." A formal written work dealing systematically with a subject.</note></term>, I have been moved, firstly, by the depletion of copies—since not a single one remains, yet there is a constant demand for it—and secondly, by its good reputation and reception, for which **GOD** be praised! Indeed, I may boldly and without hesitation write that hardly had it first saw the light of day <note>original: "an des Tages Licht gekommen," an idiom for being published.</note> when a distinguished person wished to purchase all the copies at once. ### Chapter VII.

# Of the Mineral of the Moon and its Preparation.

Just as I have done with the metals, I shall also maintain order here with the minerals, and once again bring forth the **Mineral of the Moon** <term>Minera Lunæ</term> <note>original: "Minera Lunæ"; in alchemical tradition, "Luna" (the Moon) is the universal symbol for silver</note>, or the **red-gold ore** <note>original: "roth gülden Ertzt"; historically known as pyrargyrite, a deep red mineral that is a primary source of silver</note>, for a philosophical investigation. This is a subject in which many have worked with both profit and loss; regardless of the latter, however, the pure truth still lies within it. For just as the **blessing of God** and experience in all **manipulations** <note>original: "Handgriffen"; literally "hand-grips," referring to the practical, manual skills required in a laboratory</note> make a perfect philosopher, so too can nothing harm the Art, nor make it suspect, if this or that person—perhaps due to some evil intent which they secretly harbor in their heart—is left without the blessing (upon which alone everything depends) by the omniscient God who searches the hearts and kidneys <note>original: "Hertzen und Nieren"; a biblical idiom (equivalent to "hearts and reins") referring to a person’s innermost thoughts and moral character</note>. Or, perhaps, they fail to reach a desired end due to inexperience in **labors** <note>original: "laboribus"; the physical operations and chemical experiments performed by the alchemist</note>. 

**Red-gold ore**, however, is considered the best silver ore alongside **glass-ore** <note>original: "Glaß-Ertzte"; a historical name for argentite, a dark silver mineral that can be cut with a knife like lead or wax</note>, because from time to time the greatest part of it is **native silver** <note>original: "gediegen Silber"; silver found in nature in its metallic form rather than as a compound</note>. # First true and correct preparation of silver for the preceding work.

Take one pound of **unslaked lime** <note>Also known as quicklime (calcium oxide); the author notes that even if it has already crumbled or "slaked" in the air, it will still function for this process.</note>, half a pound of common good **table salt**, and a quarter pound of raw white or red **tartar** <note>Potassium bitartrate, a sediment found in wine barrels.</note>, or as much as you wish according to this proportion. Crush everything well, mix it thoroughly together, and with this powder and fine **silver**—made into plates the thickness of the back of a knife, or rolled through a mill, or even cast in sand—place them in a **cementing box** <term>layer upon layer</term> <note>original: "stratum super stratum." A traditional alchemical term for alternating layers of metal and chemical powders.</note>.

This is done so that first, at the very bottom of the box, there is a layer of powder a good finger’s thickness, then silver, and then powder again, until everything is full; the top must also finally be covered with the same amount of powder. When another crucible or a lid is **luted** <note>Sealed with "lute," a fireproof clay or paste, to ensure the vessel is airtight.</note> upon it and everything is well dried, place it in a **cementing fire** <note>A slow, steady heat used to soak the metal in the vapors of the reagents without melting the metal itself.</note> simply between four bricks with coals. Arrange it so that the coals are all "dead" <note>original: "todt." In this context, it refers to coals that are glowing steadily without active flames, providing a consistent, smoldering heat.</note> and glow from the top down. The box—or two inverted melting crucibles luted together—should always glow a brownish-red, and no hotter, for ten to twelve hours. During this time, one must constantly add more "dead" coals as the others burn away. Then, let the fire go out, open the crucibles, and take out the metal plates, which, if the operation has proceeded well,

In this work, the following must be noted:

1. The more often one **cements** the silver, the purer it becomes of all **Venereal Soul** <note>original: "Venerischen Anima." In alchemy, the planet Venus is associated with the metal copper. This refers to removing copper impurities from the silver.</note> and superfluous moisture, and the more **fixed** <note>original: "fixer." "Fixation" refers to a substance's ability to resist the fire and not evaporate or change.</note> it becomes. Indeed, if one were to do this for an entire month out of curiosity, the salt would not only purify the silver to the highest degree, but also warm the **cold body** of the silver in such a way that ultimately no **aqua fortis** <note>original: "Aquafort." Nitric acid, which normally dissolves silver but leaves gold untouched.</note> would be able to attack it at all.

2. **Unslaked lime** <note>original: "ungelöschte Kalck." Calcium oxide.</note> is added for this reason: because it keeps the **cementing powder** loose and porous. Otherwise, the common salt would easily melt together with the silver, creating a tedious task of having to **roll it into sheets** <note>original: "laminiren."</note> over and over again.

3. It also helps the **spirits of salt** <note>original: "Spiritus Salis." Hydrochloric acid.</note> to penetrate better and to **fix** <note>original: "figiren."</note> themselves into the silver; for otherwise, spirits of salt do not dissolve silver, but only gold. When the spirits of salt are fixed into the silver, the silver will no longer be dissolved by *aqua fortis*. This also causes the metal to become dense or heavy, and to acquire a "strike" <note>The sound or feel of the metal when struck.</note> and durability—even down to the color—entirely equal to gold. 

The work itself is otherwise but **women’s work** <note>original: "Weiber-Werck." A common alchemical idiom meaning the process is easy and requires little manual labor once started.</note>, and even a child can attend to it. The costs are very low and the effect is certain. However, I do not advise undertaking this with only a few **loth** <note>A German unit of weight, roughly half an ounce.</note>, because it requires the same effort and time as if I were doing it with 100 **marks** <note>A larger unit of weight, usually about 8 ounces or 250 grams.</note>. No more is lost from the silver than the blackening moisture it carries within it; for silver still turns black when it is worn <note>The text ends on "getra-," the start of "getragen" (worn).</note> on a sweating body...

A bright red mineral (mercury sulfide) that was a foundational material in both Chinese and Western alchemy.</note> may be refined to some extent; however, no one has been willing to take the trouble to refine it in greater quantity, nor in a better way, as perhaps...

# Chapter I.

### Deals with and provides a brief repetition of the entire first part of *Alchemy Unveiled* <note>original: "Alchymiæ denudatæ." This refers to the author's earlier published work.</note>, specifically regarding metals, and simultaneously teaches wherein the true advantage actually lies.

To the reader, honored in all dignity! In the preface to the first part of my *Alchemy Unveiled*, I stated: I come here into the light of day with a treatise of which I can boast and say, without blushing, as freely as I do surely, that the like has never before reached public print. For it consists of pure and true **experiments** <note>original: "Experimentis."</note> which can lead anyone—who has even a little understanding and experience in **chemical labors** <term>Laboribus chymicis — the physical work of the laboratory, involving furnaces, vessels, and chemical reactions.</term>—to a perfect knowledge of the entire true alchemy. And that was indeed true, if only one had known how to reflect further upon the matter and had looked upon the foundation in which all true **philosophers** <term>Philosophi — the "true philosophers" or Adepts who have successfully discovered the secrets of alchemy, as opposed to common chemists.</term> unanimously agree; for truly, such a beginning would have been correct. But now I say to you, by my God and my honor (whose great name, God's, I do not misuse), in advance: that what I am writing here once again, or have written, is likewise the pure, holy

...says: I myself perhaps did not understand what I wrote in both the first part of my **Unveiled Alchemy** <note>original: "Alchymiæ denudatæ"</note> as well as the **Concordance of the Philosophers** <note>original: "Concordantia Philosophorum"</note>; however, [my critics] did not wish to better demonstrate their own understanding and experience, nor what else lies hidden behind it. For if I had not understood it, I would not have been able to reconcile everything so accurately in all my writings, nor establish the three **rotations** <term>Rotationes; successive cycles of chemical processing, such as distillation or digestion, used to purify a substance</term>. This was because Kunckel understood neither the saying of **Apelles** <note>A celebrated painter of ancient Greece</note>: "**Let the cobbler stick to his last**" <note>original: "Ne Sutor ultra crepitam" (a variation of *ultra crepidam*); a proverb warning people not to judge or offer advice beyond their area of expertise</note>, nor that no human being is perfect in all things.

Therefore, Kunckel himself was not perfect either, despite his own reminders of that fact—just as blaming, insulting, and shaming, or slandering without foundation is no art, whereas actually doing the work better certainly is. I, on the other hand, have found everything in Basilius to be true through **experience** <note>original: "Experienz"; here meaning practical laboratory experimentation</note>, provided I observed the concordance—which Kunckel also denied—and did not take his meaning literally, a mistake against which the **philosophers** <note>original: "Philosophi"; the traditional term for alchemists seeking natural wisdom</note> themselves warn. **Basilius** <note>Basilius Valentinus</note> says: Firstly, you should know that the **Tartar of the Philosophers** <term>Tartarus Philosophorum; a specialized alchemical substance, distinct from the common crust found in wine barrels</term> is not the common **cream of tartar** <note>original: "Weinstein"</note> by which the lock is opened; rather, it is another **salt**, yet it comes from the same root and is the secret key to all metals. It is made in this way: Make a **lye** <note>original: "Lauge"</note> from **vine-ash** <note>ash from the wood of grapevines</note> as sharp as possible; boil it until it is completely dry, and a reddish matter will remain. **Reverberate** <term>Reverberire; to heat a substance in a furnace where the flames are reflected back onto the material</term> this for three hours in a flaming fire, stirring it constantly until it becomes white. Afterward, **dissolve** <note>original: "solvirs"</note> it in distilled rainwater; let the **dregs** <note>original: "Feces"</note> settle well, filter it, and **coagulate** <term>Coagulire; to thicken a liquid into a solid or semi-solid state through evaporation or cooling</term> it in a glass until it is completely dry. Thus you have the **Salt of Tartar** <note>original: "Sal Tartari"</note>, from which the true **Spirit** is driven.

In this, I have been no fool; I did not believe this of common vine-ash, much less that such a thing gives the true **Spirit** <note>The volatile essence or "soul" of a substance</note> simply because he called it the **Tartar of the Philosophers** through which the lock would be opened. He adds: "That it nevertheless comes from one root and is the secret key of all metals." Because he also states that **Vitriol** <term>Vitriol; a term for various sulfate minerals or the sulfuric acid derived from them</term> alone is enough to prepare the **Philosophers' Stone** from it, I understood much more: that the **Tartar** must also come from the very same "vine-ash" [as the Vitriol]. In this belief, I was further strengthened by his **Fourth Key** <note>Refers to the "Twelve Keys of Basil Valentine," a foundational alchemical text</note>, which I—Praise GOD—also understand, as well as that which stands on page 106: <margin>96.</margin> "But to make the **Philosophers' Stone** from it (namely, from common Tartar) cannot take place; **Note Well** <note>original: "NB." or "Nota Bene"</note> because it is **vegetable** <note>original: "vegetabilisch"; meaning it belongs to the plant kingdom rather than the mineral/metallic kingdom required for the Stone</note>, etc."

Much less have I followed the literal letter...

However, those who wish to have the metals **reduced** <note>original: *reducirt*</note> into the **four elements** and claim that this is their "first matter" achieve nothing with their **reduction**.

Likewise, on page 233: And know that all metals and minerals of the earth have only a single matter and a single mother, from which they all, in their kind <note>original: *in genere*</note>, have obtained their conception and received a complete, physical birth. It is a well-known matter and the true mother of all minerals and metals; and it is a soul which unites and joins <note>original: *copulirt*</note> the spirit with the body. Such a soul is compared to water, and is also a right and true water; yet not in such a way that it wets like other water, but rather a heavenly water, dry, found in a metallic-liquid substance. It is a soulful water that loves all spirits and unites them with their corpse <note>original: *Leichnam*; in alchemy, the "corpse" refers to the solid, physical remains or "dead" body of a metal before it is "enlivened" by spirit</note> and introduces a complete life. In this, the salt is demonstrably found, which preserves against rot <note>original: *Fäule*</note> so that nothing can be consumed by corruption <note>original: *Corruption*; the natural process of decay or breaking down</note>. To speak briefly of this matter: not a few philosophers <note>original: *Philosophi*</note> say: "White makes the red"—how else could such a thing happen?—"and red makes the white." (For many a man—even when he does not yet understand the very least of it—immediately puts his fantastic whims to paper in an unscrupulous manner before he has even **worked them out** <note>original: *elaborirt*; meaning to prove through laboratory practice</note> or seen their truth or possibility, and lets them fly into the world; partly to gain a special reputation for himself, and partly perhaps to lighten the coin-purses of certain inexperienced and money-hungry misers for his own benefit—**to name examples would be distasteful** <note>original Latin: *Exempla sunt odiosa*</note>). And yet, when everything does not then proceed according to the literal word, that honest man—who himself faithfully warned against it and did not intend it as such—must be called a liar, a **process-monger** <note>original: *Process Krähmer*; a derogatory term for someone who peddles fraudulent alchemical recipes</note>, and a cheat. 

Therefore, it has certainly since been a difficult matter, and to this very day it remains no small art to distinguish the true philosophers from the false ones, and to **find one's way out of the tangle** <note>original idiom: *aus dem Krahm oder Hanffe zu finden*—literally "to find one's way out of the stall or the hemp"</note>; especially for those who are beginning, or are not yet **well-versed** in the true writings of the true philosophers, much less in...

In [these] books, much good often lies alongside [the bad]; yet there is always a snake hidden beneath for those who do not yet have a foundation. Since all true **philosophers** <note>meaning practitioners of the Hermetic Art or alchemy</note> have described their **Art** through either figures, metaphors, allegories, parables, **riddles** <note>original Latin: *Ænigmata*</note>, and the like—or even under the guise of common chemical processes, as mentioned previously—or have described the **materials** <note>original: *Materien*</note> for it according to mere color and other external appearances; then **Alexander von Suchten** <note>c. 1520–1575, a Polish chemist and physician who was a key proponent of Paracelsian medicine</note> was certainly not the only one, nor the first, to do so. 

And if his processes are found to be incorrect when followed according to the literal letter, he is not for that reason to be considered a **recipe-peddler** <note>original: *Process-Krähmer*, a derogatory term for someone who sells false or literal alchemical formulas for profit</note> or a liar. This is even less the case because, in all his writings, he consistently remains not only with the same **material** <note>original: *Materie*</note> and **method of proceeding** <note>original Latin: *modo procedendi*</note>, both in **particular** <note>original Latin: *in particulari*, referring to specific chemical operations</note> and **universal** <note>original Latin: *universali*, referring to the creation of the Philosopher's Stone</note> terms, but also frequently appeals to **Theophrastus Paracelsus** as his former teacher. Through this, along with several other good **authors** <note>original Latin: *Authoribus*</note>, he tests his writings according to the **concordance** <note>The "Concordantia Philosophorum," the principle that true masters of alchemy all agree with one another despite their different metaphors</note> as the very best guideline. 

Furthermore, as a wealthy man, he had no need for **recipe-peddling**. Otherwise, the **Great Peasant** <note>original: *der grosse Bauer*; likely a reference to the alchemical author Johannes de Monte-Snyder or a similar pseudonym common in the 17th century</note>—who so skillfully hid the true **material** for the Art under common lead, causing all the laboratory kitchens of those who followed the literal letter to be filled with common **lead ore** <note>original: *Bley-Ertz*</note>—would also have to be a fraud, simply because those people found nothing of what they sought therein; far be it from the truth!

But to come to a conclusion regarding our abandoned **Alexander von Suchten**, I would like to ask here: Who indeed is in the right? For **Lord Doctor Toxites** <note>Michael Toxites (1514–1581), a prominent physician and editor of Paracelsus</note>, **Lord von Dagiza**, **Cornelius Drebbel** <note>1572–1633, a famous Dutch inventor and alchemist</note>, and the following author in the next chapter are all four good and credible witnesses who praise him. To these, a fifth is added: namely, the famous late **Arndt** <note>Johann Arndt (1555–1621), the influential Lutheran theologian who also possessed a deep interest in Hermetic philosophy</note>, former General Superintendent of the **Duchy of Celle**. In doing so, he simultaneously corrected Morfius somewhat. I will provide these poems here only in the English language, despite them having been composed in Latin:

> The fire of the Sages destroys the living body,
> So that what was previously a stone might become a spirit;
> From its innermost core, you must tear out the gold,
> Which purifies the ores from the mother’s slime. <note>This refers to the "prima materia" or the raw, impure state of the matter before purification.</note>
> When the bones are separated from the seed,
> Then wash them with water of their own kind;
> Thus a bird grows from them, framed in many colors, <note>A reference to the "Peacock's Tail" stage of alchemy, where the matter shifts through many colors.</note>
> Which finally, hail-white, seeks its journey to heaven. <note>The "Albedo" or whitening stage.</note>
> Then paint its wings with new fire,
> Until its milk is seen to be colored truly white;
> So at last it shines upon a blood-red hill, <note>The "Rubedo" or reddening stage, marking the completion of the Philosopher's Stone.</note>
> Which yields to no fire, nor withdraws from the glow.

Thus far the work of the late **Suchten**, to which the aforementioned late **Arndt** added:

> Then, my **Morfius**, call it the wings of **Hermes**,
> Which has no equal, and is the seal of all the Sages.

### Preface of Johann Thölden.

Favorable reader! This second treatise on common antimony <note>original: "Antimonio vulgari"</note> by Alexander von Suchten, which he wrote to a nobleman, Johann Baptista von Seebachen, has never before been issued in print nor published.

->To the Noble and Excellent Lord<-
### Johann Baptista von Seebachen, etc.

Noble, honorable, especially dear Lord and good friend! My willing services with all possible diligence are always at your disposal. Upon your manifold persistence and friendly request, I cannot neglect to show you my favorable will.

Since you have a great desire and love to learn the secrets of nature <term>Heimlichkeiten der Natur: The hidden properties and occult forces within the natural world, often sought through alchemy and Hermetic philosophy.</term>, which in our times are known to few and hidden entirely in darkness—even though many of the ancients wrote about them and we still have some of their books—nevertheless, these same works are written only in a magical style <note>original: "solo stylo magico"; referring to the use of allegories, symbols, and "decknamen" or cover-names to hide secrets from the uninitiated.</note> and are of no use to anyone unless he be in the magical school

Regarding **magical antimony** <note>original: "Antimonio magico"</note>, or that of the ancients, I will mention nothing at all in this little treatise, because people want to know nothing of it; instead, everything they read, they interpret only as **common antimony** <note>original: "Antimonium"</note>, about which you desire instruction. In this writing, you should understand me only literally, for I will not use any **metaphor** <note>original: "Metaphora"</note>, **allegory** <note>original: "Allegoria"</note>, or **similitude** <note>original: "Similitudine"</note>. You might want to interject with a question here: since water multiplies the **seeds** <note>original: "Grana"</note> in the earth and is transmuted into the seeds themselves, does it follow that the **living silver** <term>Argentum vivum: Literally "living silver," the Latin term for quicksilver or mercury.</term> of metals, when multiplied with common mercury <note>original: "Mercurio vulgi"</note>, becomes a metal again? For in common mercury there is no specific essence, whereas the separative power is, by contrast, a specific essence of Mercury.

Let it stand therein for 8 days, and the amalgam will become black-gray; then pour it out and wash it clean, just as one is accustomed to washing an amalgam in a bowl. The powder that you have washed off from the amalgam, set **aside** <note>original: "ad partem"</note>. Place the amalgam back into the water bath for another 8 days, and when it has stood for that long, wash it again as you did the first time. You may perform this work 3 times, or repeat it. However, if you wish to resolve all the **copper** <note>original: "Venerem"</note> into **mercury** and **sulfur** (and perhaps also wish to have all the **gold of iron** <note>original: "Sol Martis"; literally the "Sun of Mars," referring here to a refined metallic essence extracted from iron.</note> pure out of the mercury), then you must do this work often, until the amalgam has become pure **quicksilver** <note>original: "Argento vivo"</note>, though that does not happen so quickly.

When you have had this amalgam in the bath 3 times and washed it 3 times, then distill the **quicksilver** from the **copper**, just as you previously drew it from the **silver** <note>original: "Luna"; the moon is the alchemical symbol for silver.</note>. This is called the **mercury of copper** <note>original: "Mercurium Veneris"</note>, for it is no longer **common mercury** <note>original: "Mercurius vulgi"</note>, nor **mercury of antimony**, but— <margin>Note Well <note>original: "NB."</note></margin> Note Well—it has been fermented by the mercury of copper and also **transmuted** into the mercury of copper. ### Here follows the second part concerning the Sulfur of Antimony.

Now I will also write further to you regarding what the medicine within **common antimony** <term>Antimonio vulgari: the raw mineral stibnite</term> consists of. Afterward, in conclusion, I shall fraternally share with you what can further be made from this **Regulus of Antimony** <term>Regulo Antimonii: the metallic heart or "kingly" part of the antimony ore, often appearing with a crystalline star pattern</term>; for I may truly boast that it is not unknown to me. I will write everything to you as a warning, should God grant His grace that you might understand what it is that has seduced so many people—among whom were even learned men—leading them into their own pits <note>original: "Gruben"; likely a metaphor for financial ruin or the physical dangers of toxic alchemical fumes</note> where they were taken and held captive.

Now, concerning the other part of **Antimony**, which is its **Sulfur**, you should know that it is a "fatness" <note>original: "Feistigkeit"; in alchemy, sulfur was considered the "soul" or the oily, combustible principle of a substance</note>, and it may be compared to the fire found within a black coal. Therefore, take the blackness <note>the dark residue</note> which you have washed from the **amalgam of silver** <term>Amalgama Lunæ: Luna is the alchemical symbol for silver</term> and **antimony**. Dry it in the sun, or otherwise in a gentle heat, and from it will come a lead-colored powder, to which a little **common quicksilver** <term>argenti vivi vulgi: ordinary mercury</term> still clings, having remained there during the **washing** <term>Lotione: the process of rinsing a precipitate to remove impurities</term>. If you are then able to extend <note>original: "erstrecken"; here meaning to process or calcine in a specific way</note> this powder in a closed heat—much like a **charcoal burner** <term>Kohlenbrenner: a craftsman who produces charcoal by slow-burning wood in an oxygen-starved mound</term> makes charcoal from wood—the powder will turn black and be quite similar to crushed or pulverized coal; but if you cannot process it in this way, it matters not.

Take the lead-colored powder, place it in a crucible, and set it over the fire—but do so in such a way that the crucible does not glow red, neither on the inside nor the outside. In this way, the **Mercury** <term>Mercurius: the volatile, liquid principle of the metal</term> will smoke away. The powder will then ignite from the heat, yet it does not burn with a flame like **common sulfur** <term>Sulphur: the combustible, "soul" principle</term>; instead, it glows like a dry coal that produces no flame.

Once it has burned out in this manner, a powder remains in the crucible that can be reduced back into a **Regulus** <term>the metallic heart or "kingly" part of the antimony</term>. Weigh this, and you will see how much **Antimony** <note>original: "Antimonii"</note> has been **broken down into its component parts** <note>original: "in suas partes resolviret"</note>. If you can dry the powder until it turns black and the **common mercury** <term>Mercurius vulgi</term> is removed, you can calculate precisely how much **common mercury** was contained within this **Mercury of Antimony**, and how much **burning sulfur** <term>Sulphuris urentis</term> was present in this **quicksilver** <term>Argento vivo</term>. Then you will have achieved a perfect knowledge of **Antimony**—that is, its **essential elements of quicksilver and sulfur** <note>original: "Elementum argenti vivi & Sulphuris"</note>.

**Note:** The **late Kunckel** <note>Johann von Löwenstern-Kunckel (c. 1630–1703), a famous German chemist who was often skeptical of traditional alchemical theories</note> must have neither read of this nor performed it himself—or perhaps it simply did not suit his purposes—which is why he became so hostile toward this honest pursuit. Otherwise, he would never have denied the presence of **Sulfur** within those metals.

Let this suffice as an explanation of what **Antimony** is, and how **common mercury** is **fermented and sharpened** <note>original: "fermentirt und acuirt"; 'acuirt' (acuated) refers to making a substance more chemically active or "sharp" so it can penetrate other metals</note> through and with it, so that it may also **dissolve** <term>resolviren: to break down into components</term> other metals, each according to its own kind and nature.

Alas! why do you exalt yourself, O Man, you wretched earth and ash? What is your pride and arrogance? And O holy simplicity <note>original: "ô sancta Simplicitas"</note>, how you walk in the darkness.

For this reason, I would faithfully advise each and every person that they should certainly go to school and learn first, before they set themselves up as Teachers <term>Præceptores; instructors or masters of a subject</term>, judge others, or wish to begin working in **Alchemy**. For only he is truly experienced in the **Art** who has properly learned it; but if he has not yet learned it, then he can neither know nor understand it, nor find fault with others. Conclude, therefore, with **Basilius** <note>Basilius Valentinus, the purported Benedictine monk and author of influential alchemical texts like "The Triumphal Chariot of Antimony"</note> on page 59: The highest planet of the heavens, called **Saturn** <note>In alchemy, Saturn represents the metal lead, but in the context of Basilius and Kunckel, it often refers to the "hidden" qualities of antimony</note> (and indeed the one known to Kunckel as a weed), has the most undervalued authority in our mastery <term>Meisterschafft; the completion or expert practice of the Great Work</term>, and is nonetheless—**Note Well! Note Well!** <note>original: "NB. NB." for the Latin "Nota Bene"</note>—the foremost key of the entire **Art**, assigned to our **Art** by God and Nature. And although he has soared to the highest heights above all lights through his swift flight, he must nevertheless be brought down to the very lowest separation and come into improvement through his combustion.

<meta>This page continues the argument regarding the true nature of antimony, specifically addressing the misconceptions held by those who do not understand the underlying "Principles of the Art." It follows the previous page's transition into a defense of alchemical mastery against skeptics like Kunckel.</meta>

( 0 )

Although much has been written by the **Philosophers** about **Antimony** <term>Antimonio; a metallic element used in alchemical processes, believed to hold the key to the Philosopher's Stone</term>, it is nonetheless all without foundation, as none of them treats it sincerely and completely. This is because the highest secret consists partly in it, and in other parts completely, when I distinguish between the **common antimony** <note>original: "Antimonio vulgi"</note> and the **magical antimony** <note>original: "Antimonio magico"</note>. What others—aside from the true **Philosophers**—write about it is entirely without foundation. For how can someone write anything correct who is ignorant of both the **Principles of Things** <note>original: "Principia Rerum"</note> and the **Principles of the Art** <note>original: "Principia Artis"</note>? (Among which there is nonetheless a great difference; for although they also posit that the **Principles of Nature** <note>original: "Principia Naturæ"</note> are also the **Principles of the Art**, this is only to be understood in a certain sense). 

Regarding this, **Theophrastus** <note>Theophrastus Bombastus von Hohenheim, known as Paracelsus (1493–1541), a famous physician and alchemist</note> gave an example of wood for a better understanding, by which he shows that the three **Principles** <note>The "Tria Prima": Mercury, Sulfur, and Salt, which Paracelsus believed were the fundamental components of all matter</note> are hidden in all things. But he nevertheless teaches the **Principles of the Art** as little as he teaches the **Principles of Nature**. For when wood burns, its **Mercury** <note>original: "Mercurius"; in alchemy, this represents the volatile or "spirit" principle</note> indeed passes away, but not simply <note>original: "simpliciter"</note>; rather, a part of it passes away with it.

The **Sulfur** <note>original: "Schweffel"; the principle of combustibility or the "soul"</note> is also not separated, for the fire completely destroys the **compound** <note>original: "Compositum"</note>. The **Salt** <note>original: "Salz"; the principle of stability or the "body"</note>, however, which remains in the ashes, is reduced by the fire to a coarse matter, and not that [divine essence] from which all things are made.

Thus it is also a poor art to extract the water from a herb, then to drive off the oil from it, and finally to make salt from the dregs <note>original: "Fecibus"</note>; which three, however, are for that reason neither **Salt, Sulfur, nor Mercury** <note>The "Tria Prima" or three primary elements of Paracelsian alchemy</note> of either nature or art. (And indeed just as little as **Kunckel's** <note>Johannes Kunckel (c. 1630–1703) was a famous German chemist and alchemist known for his work on glass-making and his skeptical approach to traditional alchemy</note> **Mercury, Salt, and Earth** <note>original: "Mercurius, Sal und Terra"</note> are the true **Principles of Nature** <note>original: "Principia Naturæ"</note> or of the Art. For the way he teaches how to make **Mercury** <note>original: "Mercurium"</note>, it remains nonetheless a metal—no matter from which metal it is extracted—and it is at the same time a dead body <note>original: "todes Corpus"; referring to matter that has lost its vital alchemical spirit</note>, and therefore not a **Principle** <note>original: "Principium"</note>. The salt, likewise, only became a salt through the fire and not by nature; thus it is again neither the salt of nature nor of art, because it is simultaneously also a dead body. And the earth <note>original: "Erde"</note> that he establishes is a burnt, sulfurous viscous substance <note>original: "sulphurisches Viscosum"</note> in which nature does not operate at all. It is therefore even less useful for the Art or as a **Principle**. Thus, all three are dead bodies <note>original: "tode Corpora"</note> in which nature can work neither by itself <note>original: "per se"</note> nor through the assistance of the Art for all eternity. For the water carries over with it what is subtle from the other two; likewise, the oil does not go without the water when the **dry** <note>original: "Siccum"</note> is drawn from the **moist** <note>original: "Humido"</note>. These two, furthermore, cannot mix without the air—**Note Well** <note>original: "NB."</note> that is, the salt. But the salt that is drawn from the dregs <note>original: "Fecibus"</note> is a burnt **earth** <note>original: "Terra"</note>, and thus the three are not simple bodies <note>original: "simplicia corpora"</note>).

From the <term>macrocosm</term> <note>the "great world" or universe</note> and <term>microcosm</term> <note>the "little world" or the human body, which was believed to mirror the universe</note> many kinds of diseases now arise. These can be conveniently divided into five classes based on their causes:

1) Some are supernaturally imposed by **GOD**, for which only a zealous and humble prayer of faith may be of assistance. Paracelsus calls the origin of such diseases: the **Divine Influence** <note>original Latin: "Ens Deale," referring to the first of Paracelsus's five "Entia" or origins of disease</note>.

2) There are **diseases brought about by unclean spirits with God's permission** <note>original Latin: "Morbi permissu Dei à Spiritibus immundis illati"</note>, in which prayer must also perform the best work. However, because evil spirits commonly cause illness and harm through natural means, natural counter-remedies and medicines can also be used here, of which many books and writings are otherwise available. According to Paracelsus, the cause of such diseases is the **Demonic Influence** <note>original: "Ens pagoycum," a term used by Paracelsus to describe illnesses rooted in spiritual or magical forces</note>.

3) **Astral diseases** <note>original Latin: "Morbi astrales"</note> also arise from the **malignant emissions of the stars** <note>original Latin: "Effluviis malignis astrorum"</note>, through which the air is filled and malignant diseases are caused in people. Very little has yet been written regarding the cures for these diseases. Paracelsus calls the cause of such diseases the **Astral Influence** <note>original Latin: "Ens astrale"</note>.

4) Human nature—and thus every individual human being—is predisposed toward disease and death through the first **curse** <note>original Latin: "Malediction"</note> in Paradise and the subsequent one through the **Great Flood** <note>original German: "Sündfluth"</note>. Through these, a limit has been set for the general human course of life, which one may not exceed. Beyond this corruption, further particular decay arises in a person, not only

...attentiveness; because the work is somewhat dangerous, the <term>Oil of Vitriol</term> <note>original Latin: *Oleum Vitrioli*; concentrated sulfuric acid, a primary reagent in alchemy</note> releases the water it attracted from the air and seizes, in place of its first lost combustible oiliness <note>original: *Fettigkeit*; in alchemical theory, "fatness" or "oiliness" refers to the sulfurous principle of combustibility and soul within a substance</note> of the turpentine, and thereby becomes once again a burning sulfur, as before. This is especially true since in my aforementioned **masterpiece** <term>Meisterstücke</term> and **final farewell** <term>ultimo vale</term> <note>original: *ultimo vale*. A Latin expression for a final work or a parting greeting before death.</note>, which is yet to be released freely, I deal primarily with the whole, complete **process** <term>Process</term> of the **procedure** <term>Procedur</term> <note>The "Process" refers to the specific laboratory steps required to achieve the Great Work.</note>—something which no author has yet done since the world began, as I can say with truth, and from which the truth shall indeed be seen. 

And what would become of it if such wicked rogues, as well as honest folk, were to get everything into their hands—they who know how to boast loudly enough with their deceptions? Where would the respect and preference for the ancient as well as the modern Sages remain? Where honor and integrity? Where virtue and vice? Especially since even tailors and bakers' apprentices <note>The author is expressing a common period elitism, arguing that common laborers should stay in their "God-given" trades rather than dabbling in the high art of alchemy.</note> run to it and hang the station in which **GOD** placed them on a nail <note>A German idiom meaning to abandon or quit one's profession.</note>. 

But as for those who are honest and brave people, I wish to serve them still, for a good remembrance of my humble self after my death in my grave, for a proper fee—but especially those who have already been my benefactors, as mentioned previously. This is so that they may recognize my grateful spirit even from that which **GOD** has further bestowed upon me since then. For which, to Him, the Triune, eternal, and immortal **GOD**, be eternal praise, honor, and thanks said herewith and into all eternity, for everything He has shown to His unworthy creature from youth onwards, and will further do until my end. 

I am now entering my 67th year; and because our life lasts 70 years, and if it comes to much, 80 <note>A biblical reference to Psalm 90:10 regarding the typical human lifespan.</note>, it might not last that much longer, unless the dear **GOD** should show me some further grace through the **Universal Medicine** <term>Universal-Medicin</term> <note>The Philosopher's Stone in its role as a panacea or life-extending elixir.</note>. I have likewise resolved to diligently record its use and effect—since the **philosophers** <term>Philosophi</term> have left so very little specifically concerning this—and to charge someone during my lifetime to publish it after my death. With which, for this time,

->also let this be the<-

## T  H  E    E  N  D.

<summary>The author concludes his work by defending the secrecy of the alchemical process from the lower classes and rogues, while thanking God for his 67 years of life. He expresses his intent to document the physical effects of the Universal Medicine, as he feels previous masters neglected to describe its practical use.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discussion of alchemical authorities and the specific order of planetary metals as described by Michael Sendivogius.</meta>

*Sendivogius* in the *New Chemical Light* <note>original Latin: *Novum Lumen Chymicum*</note>, page 570, sets the *generation of metals* <term>generation of metals: the alchemical theory that metals "grow" in the earth from a seed-like state toward the perfection of gold.</term> in the following order:

Saturn [Lead] ♄, Jupiter [Tin] ♃, Mars [Iron] ♂, Sun [Gold] ☉, Venus [Copper] ♀, Mercury [Quicksilver] ☿, Moon [Silver] ☽.

Other *philosophers* <note>In the early modern period, "philosophers" almost always referred to alchemists, who sought the "Philosopher's Stone."</note> however, set the following order, which is considered correct:

Saturn [Lead] ♄, Jupiter [Tin] ♃, Moon [Silver] ☽, Venus [Copper] ♀, Mercury [Quicksilver] ☿, Mars [Iron] ♂, Sun [Gold] ☉.

Note Well: *Michael Sendivogius* has hidden his name in the following *anagram*:

->*I love the divine Polish race.* <note>original Latin: *Divi leschi genus Amo*. This is a famous anagram where the letters can be rearranged to spell *Michael Sendivogius*.</note><-

<summary>This page compares two different alchemical sequences for the "generation of metals" and provides the famous Latin anagram used by the Polish alchemist Michael Sendivogius to conceal his identity.</summary>
<keywords>Michael Sendivogius, alchemy, generation of metals, planetary symbols, anagram, Novum Lumen Chymicum, history of chemistry</keywords>
